name: numen.build.place
signature: fun(design: Cells|Blueprint): Placed Make the cells of a design that your hand reaches from where you stand look like it: each such cell gets its turn once.
brief: Make the cells of a design that your hand reaches from where you stand look like it: each such cell gets its turn once.
helpText:
---Make the cells of a design that your hand reaches from where you stand look like it: each such cell gets its turn once.
---@param design Cells|Blueprint What it should look like: Cells (each a Block, the block for that cell written as /setblock takes it), or a Blueprint from numen.build.blueprint.
---@return Placed
function numen.build.place(design) end
-- Examples:
--   numen.build.place({{name = "cobblestone", pos = {x = 100, y = 64, z = -20}}, {name = "oak_stairs[facing=east]", pos = {x = 101, y = 64, z = -20}}})
--   numen.build.place({{name = "crafting_table", pos = {x = 101, y = 64, z = -20}}})
--   numen.build.place(numen.build.blueprint("tower", {x = 100, y = 64, z = -20}))
-- Notes:
--   It never walks and never digs: it places only the cells within reach of where you stand, each once, then returns how many it placed and how many are left. `numen.build.diff` says what is still to do and where; `numen.build.raise` (library) walks the site, digs what is in the way and calls this until the whole building stands.
--   Background work: fails at once with kind out_of_reach when nothing of it is within reach to place, with how many cells are left and a hint with the numen.move.to call to the lowest nearest one; nothing starts. When everything already looks like it, it returns at once with nothing placed.
--   A blueprint at the same dimension, spot and rotation is the same building: placing it again adds what is missing, replaces what differs, and removes only blocks you placed there before that the file no longer has and that nobody has changed since. Cells are only those cells.
--   Survival: Cells are priced as a whole before the first block and refused, placing nothing, when anything is short; a blueprint builds as far as your stock goes. Where another block stands it places nothing: dig it out first with numen.work.dig (numen.build.diff lists those cells). Creative replaces it at once.
--   Asks your owner first when their rules say so, for the cells it would change; a refusal stops it with their words.
-- See also: numen.build.diff, numen.build.raise, numen.task.stop

name: numen.build.raise
signature: fun(building: Cells|Blueprint, opts?: table): integer Build Cells or a Blueprint (from numen.build.blueprint) until all of it went in.
brief: Build Cells or a Blueprint (from numen.build.blueprint) until all of it went in. Each round asks numen.build.diff what
helpText:
---Build Cells or a Blueprint (from numen.build.blueprint) until all of it went in. Each round asks numen.build.diff what
---is still to do from where you stand, then places what is within reach (numen.build.place), or digs out the blocks in
---the way (numen.move.to with arrive "dig", then numen.work.dig), or walks within reach of the lowest nearest cell left
---(numen.move.to with arrive "place"). Drops of what it digs stay where they fall: numen.work.collect() picks them up.
---A walk that stops short (no_path) ends its round and the next round plans again from where you stand. A round that
---leaves everything as it was raises failed with what is left (and why the last walk stopped), and so do cells nothing
---holds once all else stands; any other step that fails raises its own error.
---@param building Cells|Blueprint What to build.
---@param opts? table The description for the walks (costs = {dig = true, place = true} lets it pillar up to high cells and dig its way).
---@return integer rounds How many rounds it took.
function numen.build.raise(building, opts) end

helpText:
---Attack one entity until it is dead, lost or out of reach.
---@param entity integer|Entity The entity to fight: an Entity from numen.scan.entities, or its id.
---@return Fought
function numen.fight.attack(entity) end
-- Examples:
--   numen.fight.attack(184)
--   local r = numen.fight.attack(184)
--   print(r.strikes, #r.fought)
-- Notes:
--   Several: `for _, foe in ipairs(numen.scan.entities("hostile", {radius = 16})) do numen.fight.attack(foe) end`; `numen.fight.clear()` (library) does that until none is left.
--   Background work: it keeps chasing, turning, swinging, shooting and dodging until that one is dead, gone or out of reach, and returns then.
--   The body picks how: it closes in and swings when it can reach, shoots with a bow or crossbow when it cannot, keeps its distance from things that explode, and picks the weapon you own that is strongest against that target.
--   It does not pick up what the target drops: `numen.work.collect()` does. Things that split (slimes, magma cubes) come back as new ids: scan again, or `numen.fight.clear()`.
--   Asks your owner before hitting a pet, a named mob or a villager when their rules say so.
-- See also: numen.scan.entities, numen.fight.clear, numen.work.collect, numen.task.stop

---Modules — functions written in Lua 5.2 that programs use by name, kept as files on your owner's computer (numen/work.lua is numen.work): the built-in ones, your own, and how the programs that used them went.
---@class numen.module

---@field list fun(): ModuleInfo[] The modules: what each does, whose it is, how the programs that used it went.
---@field reset fun(name: string) Put a built-in module back as it shipped with this version: your changes go, a deleted one comes back.

---@field last_run? integer When a program last used it, epoch milliseconds.
---@field failed_line? integer The line the last unfinished program stopped at.
---@field failed_why? string Why it stopped there.

---@field factory boolean Whether the text is the one it shipped with.
---@field code string The whole module.

helpText:
---Keep a module under a name: programs then use its functions by that name. Saving under a built-in module's name changes that module.
---@param code string The module: a first comment line saying what it does, functions put in a table, and that table returned (local M = {} … function M.chop(tree) … end … return M).
---@param opts? numen.module.save.opts
---@return Saved
function numen.module.save(code, opts) end

---@class numen.module.save.opts
---@field name? string Name to keep it under, the name programs use it by: namespace.group, each lowercase letters, digits and _ (my.lumber for one of your own; numen.work changes that built-in one). Omit to give it the next free name my.module_1, my.module_2, ….
-- Examples:
--   numen.module.save([[
--   -- Clearing a pit.
--   local M = {}
--   ---Dig out every block given.
--   function M.clear(blocks)
--     numen.work.dig(blocks)
--   end
--   return M
--   ]], {name = "my.pit"})
-- Notes:
--   Instant. The module is read and loaded once first, and not kept if it does not compile, does not return a table, or redefines an API function; the error says the line. Its first line is a comment saying what it does, and the comment lines above each function say what that one does: that is how the list and numen.api.help describe them.
--   A module named after an API group (numen.move, numen.work, ...) adds its functions to that group. Saving under a name that has a file replaces it and resets its record. Your owner can edit the files too; the next program reads them as they are.
-- See also: numen.module.delete, numen.module.reset

brief: Aim at a block, fluid or air cell within reach and right-click it: the full native click. When it opens a window (a chest, a furnace, a machine) it returns that Window.
helpText:
---Aim at a block, fluid or air cell within reach and right-click it: the full native click. When it opens a window (a chest, a furnace, a machine) it returns that Window.
---@param cell Pos The cell to aim at.
---@param opts? numen.use.block.opts
---@return Window|Clicked
function numen.use.block(cell, opts) end

---@class numen.use.block.opts
---@field hold? number How long to hold the button, in seconds (up to 60); the press ends early once the action completes. Omit to press once.
---@field item? string An item from your inventory to take in hand first, e.g. minecraft:bone_meal. Omit to use what you hold.
---@field sneak? boolean Hold sneak while pressing, as a player holds Shift and clicks; while riding, that steps you off first (numen.move.dismount() does just that). Omit to press standing.
-- Examples:
--   local w = numen.use.block({x = 120, y = 64, z = -35})
--   numen.use.block({x = 120, y = 63, z = -35}, {item = "minecraft:bucket"})
--   numen.use.block({x = 120, y = 64, z = -35}, {item = "minecraft:oak_planks", sneak = true})
-- Notes:
--   When the click opens a window, it returns the Window, the same as numen.gui.view(): its methods put, take, move, quick and close work on it (see the numen.gui group).
--   If the aimed block doesn't take a right click, the held item acts on its own, exactly like a real right-click: aiming at water with a bucket scoops it, with a boat places it.
--   With sneak = true and something in hand, a right click skips what the aimed block itself does: a block goes onto a chest instead of opening it.
--   It does NOT travel: you must already be within working reach (~4.5 blocks) of the aim point; `numen.move.to({x = 120, y = 64, z = -35}, {arrive = "use"})` stands you where one of its faces is in sight and in reach. Farther away it fails and names that call.
--   It is a bare key press: whatever you hold is what is used, and the block the crosshair lands on is the one clicked — if something else is in the way (tall grass in front of a chest, a leaf), that is what gets clicked, and the result says so and names the next step. It never moves, never swaps tools, never clears the way.
--   Placing near your owner's things may ask your owner first; the call waits for the answer.
--   Otherwise the result reports what actually changed (your inventory and experience, health, riding, the aimed block, new entities); no change listed means the click did nothing.
-- See also: numen.gui.view, numen.use.hit, numen.use.entity

name: numen.work.dig
signature: fun(blocks: Pos|Block|(Pos|Block): [], opts?: {count?: integer}): Dug Dig the given blocks that are within reach of where you stand.
brief: Dig the given blocks that are within reach of where you stand.
notes: 单格 ~1.7s（泥土手挖）；掉落常在脚下自动拾取；不走路
helpText:
---Dig the given blocks that are within reach of where you stand.
---@param blocks Pos|Block|(Pos|Block)[] What to dig, as many as you like: a Block from a query is dug only while that cell still holds that block; a Pos is dug whatever it holds, air and fluid skipped; a Cluster from numen.scan.blocks is its blocks.
---@param opts? numen.work.dig.opts
---@return Dug
function numen.work.dig(blocks, opts) end

---@class numen.work.dig.opts
---@field count? integer How many cells to dig at most (up to 256). Omit to dig every cell of it within reach.
-- Examples:
--   numen.work.dig({name = "minecraft:iron_ore", pos = {x = 120, y = 12, z = -35}}, {name = "minecraft:iron_ore", pos = {x = 121, y = 12, z = -35}})
--   numen.work.dig({x = 120, y = 12, z = -35})
--   local r = numen.work.dig({{x = 120, y = 64, z = -35}, {x = 120, y = 65, z = -35}}, {count = 1})
--   print(r.dug, r.left, r.out_of_reach)
-- Notes:
--   A cluster from `numen.scan.blocks` or a Block from `numen.scan.block` goes in as it is.
--   Digs only what your hand reaches from where you stand: it never walks and never picks up. Get within reach first with `numen.move.to(cluster, {arrive = "dig"})` (it picks the spot that reaches the most cells), dig, and pick up what it dropped: `local r = numen.work.dig({x = 120, y = 12, z = -35}); numen.work.collect({items = r.drops})`; `numen.work.mine(cluster)` does all three until the cluster is gone.
--   Before it returns it waits up to 2 seconds for what this dig dropped to settle, and says where each went: landed (and where), picked up (and by whom), destroyed (lava, fire, a cactus …), fallen into the void, or still moving. Only what it dropped is followed, and only until it settles.
--   Background work: before it starts it checks something within reach can be dug, harvested with your tools and is allowed; when nothing is, it fails with kind out_of_reach (or denied, failed) and a hint with the numen.move.to call to copy — no task starts and whatever you were doing goes on. It returns when the job ends: how many cells it dug and how many are still out of reach, the nearest of them as a pos.
--   A block in the way of your hand is dug open too when it is natural terrain. A block in the way that needs your owner's consent or that their rules forbid is not touched: the account names it, where it is and why.
--   Takes the best tool for each block; only digs what your tools actually harvest, and says so when nothing qualifies. Asks your owner before breaking a named block their rules want asked about; a refusal stops the job with the reason.
-- See also: numen.move.to, numen.work.collect, numen.scan.blocks, numen.task.stop
